name: Press Fit
description: Parts are forced together, friction holds them
clearance_note: Depends on printer accuracy, material, and nominal dimension. Typically -0.1 to -0.2mm interference for FDM.
design_notes: Add a chamfer to aid insertion
fdm_considerations: FDM parts have anisotropic strength; press fit direction matters. Compressing layers is better than pulling them apart.

name: Sliding Fit
description: Parts can move relative to each other with minimal play
clearance_note: Usually requires +0.1mm to +0.2mm clearance depending on machine calibration.
design_notes: Use a larger clearance for longer sliding surfaces to prevent binding
fdm_considerations: Layer lines increase friction. Orient parts so layer lines are parallel to sliding direction if possible.

name: Clearance Fit
description: Parts assemble freely with intentional gap
design_notes: If parts must spin freely, err on the side of larger clearances (>0.3mm)
fdm_considerations: Z-seams can cause bumps that interfere with clearance fits. Align seams away from moving surfaces.

name: Snap Fit
description: Flexible features deflect and lock into place
clearance_note: Clearance at the locking face is usually 0.1mm to 0.2mm to ensure a tight lock.
design_notes: Avoid sharp corners at the base of the snap arm to prevent fatigue
fdm_considerations: Crucial to print snap arms with layer lines running along the length of the arm, not across it, to prevent snapping.

name: Screw Fit / Printed Threads
description: Parts are joined using standard threaded geometry printed directly
clearance_note: Apply a negative horizontal expansion or clearance of ~0.1-0.2mm to the thread profile.
design_notes: Use a standard thread profile but scale clearance
Custom coarse threads are easier to print than fine standard threads
fdm_considerations: Fine threads (<M6) are very difficult to print cleanly. Print threads vertically for best resolution.

name: Heat-Set Insert
description: Metal threaded inserts melted into the plastic part
clearance_note: Hole diameter should be slightly smaller than the insert outer diameter (see manufacturer specs).
design_notes: Ensure sufficient wall thickness around the insert
Hole depth should be slightly deeper than the insert
fdm_considerations: Works exceptionally well with thermoplastics like PLA, PETG, ABS. Requires a soldering iron for installation.
